summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into their query and processing layers, enabling teams to run embeddings, LLM inference, and vector similarity search without moving data to external systems. Vector search has become a defining feature, with 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on it by 2026 and adoption growing 377% year over year. The competitive landscape spans purpose-built vector databases, Postgres extensions like pgvector, and fully integrated cloud data platforms that bundle model serving, RAG pipelines, and governance into a single service.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless AI functions running directly inside the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. Capabilities include LLM-powered text-to-SQL, summarization, sentiment analysis, translation, embedding generation (EMBED_TEXT), and retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. As of early 2026, Snowflake Postgres runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates with Cortex AI for embedding generation and text-to-SQL, while also supporting pgvector for vector similarity search within Postgres instances. Cortex Search and Cortex Analyst provide managed semantic search and natural-language BI query layers respectively.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native vector search is available via Cortex Search, a fully managed hybrid (vector + keyword) search service built into Snowflake. Additionally, Snowflake Postgres natively integrates pgvector, bringing vector similarity search to Postgres instances running inside the AI Data Cloud without requiring separate infrastructure. Both paths are considered native to the Snowflake platform.
databases.llm_integration: Cortex AI hosts and serves multiple LLMs (including Meta Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake Arctic) directly within Snowflake's security boundary. Users call models via SQL functions such as COMPLETE(), EMBED_TEXT_768(), and SUMMARIZE(). No data leaves the Snowflake environment, satisfying enterprise governance requirements.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits per token processed. Cortex Search has a separate per-query and storage cost. Pricing varies by model size and region; larger models (e.g., Llama 3.1 405B) consume significantly more credits per call than smaller models. Snowflake Postgres is generally available soon as of February 2026 with its own compute credit billing.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to create and execute machine learning models directly in BigQuery using SQL, covering classification, regression, time-series forecasting, matrix factorization, and boosted trees. Beyond classic ML, BigQuery integrates deeply with Vertex AI, enabling users to call Vertex-hosted foundation models (Gemini, text-embedding, and others) via the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT SQL functions. BigQuery also supports Vector Search as a first-class feature, allowing semantic similarity queries over embedding columns stored in BigQuery tables. Remote functions can invoke any Vertex AI or Cloud Run endpoint, making the platform extensible to custom models.
databases.vector_search_notes: BigQuery has native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH SQL function (GA as of 2024, actively developed into 2026). It supports approximate nearest-neighbor search over ARRAY<FLOAT64> embedding columns stored directly in BigQuery tables, with no external database or extension required. Indexes can be created natively for performance at scale.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Google Vertex AI and the Gemini model family. Users call ML.GENERATE_TEXT or ML.EMBED_TEXT in SQL, pointing to a Vertex AI remote model resource. Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0, text-embedding-004, and multimodal embedding models are all accessible. Connections are managed via BigQuery Connection resources with IAM-based security.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference are billed on top of standard BigQuery compute (slots or on-demand per-TB scanned). Calls to Vertex AI foundation models through BigQuery incur Vertex AI token-based pricing in addition to BigQuery query costs. Vector Search index storage and query compute are billed separately. Free tier allows limited BigQuery ML usage each month.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: PostgreSQL itself has no built-in AI/ML engine, but the open-source extension ecosystem provides powerful capabilities. pgvector adds vector similarity search (exact and approximate nearest-neighbor via HNSW and IVFFlat indexes) directly to any Postgres instance, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search — no new infrastructure, same security model, same backup procedures. pgai (from Timescale) further extends Postgres with SQL functions to call external LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere, Anthropic) for embedding generation, text completion, and RAG pipeline orchestration directly from SQL. For most teams, pgvector on Postgres is recommended as the default starting point for RAG in 2026, handling up to 50 million vectors effectively.
databases.vector_search_notes: Vector search is available via the pgvector open-source extension, which must be installed into the Postgres instance (self-hosted or managed). While it is an extension rather than a core Postgres built-in, pgvector is so widely adopted and available on virtually all managed Postgres services (RDS, Cloud SQL, Supabase, Neon, etc.) that it is considered the standard Postgres vector search solution. HNSW indexes provide approximate nearest-neighbor performance suitable for tens of millions of vectors.
databases.llm_integration: The pgai extension provides SQL-callable functions that proxy to external LLM APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama (local), and Cohere. Embedding generation can be automated via pgai vectorizer, which watches tables and keeps embedding columns current. Snowflake Postgres additionally integrates with Snowflake Cortex for managed LLM access within the AI Data Cloud.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Costs depend entirely on the underlying Postgres hosting (self-managed is infrastructure cost only; managed services like Supabase or Neon charge compute and storage). LLM calls via pgai are billed by the respective LLM provider at their standard API token rates. Snowflake Postgres incurs Snowflake credit costs.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables Aurora MySQL-Compatible and Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible databases to invoke external AWS AI/ML services directly from SQL queries using familiar SELECT statements. Supported integrations include Amazon SageMaker (for custom trained models) and Amazon Comprehend (for NLP tasks such as sentiment detection and entity recognition). Predictions are returned as SQL query results, allowing ML inference to be embedded in application queries without moving data out of Aurora. This is a pass-through integration model — Aurora sends data to external AWS services and returns results — rather than in-database model execution.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora does not have native built-in vector search. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is possible only by installing the pgvector extension, which is supported on Aurora PostgreSQL. Because pgvector is a third-party extension (not a native Aurora feature), vector_search is marked false for Aurora itself. Users who need vector search on Aurora should enable the pgvector extension on Aurora PostgreSQL instances.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon SageMaker endpoints (including SageMaker-hosted foundation models and Jumpstart models) and Amazon Comprehend via SQL function calls. As Amazon Bedrock has grown, some architectures invoke Bedrock from Lambda triggered by Aurora events, but direct Bedrock invocation from Aurora SQL is not a native supported feature as of 2026. SageMaker integration supports any model deployed to a real-time inference endpoint.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML itself does not add a separate line-item cost to Aurora; standard Aurora compute and storage pricing applies. However, each SQL-based ML prediction call invokes the target AWS service (SageMaker or Comprehend), which is billed at that service's standard inference pricing. SageMaker endpoint costs depend on instance type and hours running. Comprehend is priced per unit of text processed.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Amazon Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to create, train, and invoke machine learning models using SQL commands directly within Redshift. Under the hood, Redshift ML uses Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train and tune models on data exported from Redshift, then imports the resulting model artifact back into Redshift as a SQL function. Users call predictions via SELECT statements using the auto-generated model function. Supported problem types include binary and multi-class classification, regression, and time-series forecasting. Redshift ML also supports bringing pre-trained SageMaker models (BYOM) for inference within Redshift queries, and integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM-powered text functions in newer releases.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift does not have native built-in vector search or a supported vector search extension. Redshift is a columnar OLAP data warehouse not architected for approximate nearest-neighbor vector indexing. Teams needing vector search alongside Redshift data typically use a separate purpose-built vector database (Pinecone, OpenSearch, pgvector on RDS/Aurora) and join results at the application layer or via Redshift federated queries.
databases.llm_integration: Redshift ML integrates with SageMaker Autopilot for automated model training and SageMaker endpoints for BYOM inference. Newer Redshift ML capabilities include integration with Amazon Bedrock, allowing SQL-callable functions for text generation and embedding using Bedrock-hosted foundation models (Titan, Claude, Llama). This enables RAG-adjacent workflows where Redshift data is passed to an LLM and results returned in SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML training jobs are billed based on SageMaker Autopilot training time and instance usage, in addition to standard Redshift costs. Data transfer from Redshift to S3 (used as the training data staging area) may incur S3 costs. Inference via BYOM uses SageMaker endpoint pricing. Bedrock-based LLM calls within Redshift are billed at Bedrock token pricing per invocation.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks has consolidated its AI/ML offerings under the Mosaic AI brand, covering the full lifecycle from data preparation to model training, fine-tuning, serving, and evaluation. Mosaic AI includes MLflow for experiment tracking, Model Serving for real-time inference endpoints, AI Playground for LLM exploration, and Agent Framework for building production RAG and AI agent applications. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector database built into the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, allowing teams to create vector indexes directly on Delta Lake tables and query them for semantic similarity — with automatic sync as underlying data changes. Databricks also integrates with pgvector and notes pgvector compatibility for teams using Postgres alongside Databricks for analytics.
databases.vector_search_notes: Databricks Vector Search is a native, fully managed vector search service built into the Databricks platform (not a third-party extension). It creates and maintains vector indexes on top of Delta Lake tables, supports real-time sync when source data changes, and provides both Python SDK and REST API query interfaces. Approximate nearest-neighbor search uses a managed index with no infrastructure for users to operate.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts open-source and fine-tuned LLMs (Llama, Mistral, DBRX, and others) on Databricks-managed GPU infrastructure with pay-per-token pricing. Foundation Model APIs provide access to Databricks-curated LLMs via a standard OpenAI-compatible API. External model integrations allow routing to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Amazon Bedrock endpoints through a unified gateway. AI Functions in SQL (AI_GENERATE_TEXT, AI_EMBED) allow LLM inference directly from Spark SQL or Databricks notebooks.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks Vector Search is billed in Databricks Units (DBUs) based on the number of vector index entries and query volume, with a serverless consumption model. Mosaic AI Model Serving is priced per token for Foundation Model APIs, with rates varying by model. Custom model serving on dedicated endpoints is billed by instance-hour. MLflow and experiment tracking are included with Databricks workspace at no additional per-feature charge.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI capabilities
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic similarity search directly on documents stored in Atlas collections by indexing embedding fields using hierarchical navigable small world (HNSW) algorithm. It is integrated into the Atlas Search infrastructure and queried via the $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline stage, making it a native part of MongoDB query operations without requiring a separate system. Atlas also integrates with major AI frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Semantic Kernel, and supports connections to external LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Cohere) for embedding generation and RAG pipelines. MongoDB Atlas is listed among the top enterprise vector database solutions for 2026, particularly valued for teams already using MongoDB who want to add vector search without adopting a new database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Atlas Vector Search is a native built-in feature of MongoDB Atlas, available on M10 and larger cluster tiers and on Atlas Serverless. It does not require any extension or separate service — vector indexes are created and managed through the Atlas UI, Atlas CLI, or MongoDB drivers using the same tooling as standard Atlas Search indexes. The $vectorSearch aggregation operator is part of the MongoDB query language.
databases.llm_integration: MongoDB Atlas does not host LLMs internally but provides native integrations with external AI services and frameworks. The Atlas AI Data API and official LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations make it straightforward to build RAG pipelines where MongoDB stores both documents and their embeddings. Atlas Charts and the broader Atlas platform support AI-assisted query generation in preview. MongoDB Compass (the GUI) has begun incorporating AI-powered query generation features.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included with Atlas clusters at M10 tier and above; there is no separate per-query charge for vector search itself. Costs are driven by Atlas cluster compute and storage pricing. Serverless Atlas instances support vector search with consumption-based billing per read/write processing unit. Vector index storage counts against Atlas storage quotas. LLM API calls for embedding generation are billed separately by the external provider.
